description: The map n to the integer class of (n,0) is injective and preserves addition, multiplication, zero, one, and order.
signature:
Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.natural_integer_embedding :
  (Function.Injective fun n => Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerClass n 0) ∧
    (∀ (m n : ℕ),
        Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerAdd
            (Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerClass m 0)
            (Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerClass n 0) =
          Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerClass (m + n) 0) ∧
      (∀ (m n : ℕ),
          Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerMul
              (Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerClass m 0)
              (Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerClass n 0) =
            Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerClass (m * n) 0) ∧
        (∀ (m n : ℕ),
            Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.IntegerLE
                (Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerClass m 0)
                (Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerClass n 0) ↔
              m ≤ n) ∧
          Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerValue
                (Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerClass 0 0) =
              0 ∧
            Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerValue
                (Lemmatheca.Entry.ConstructingNumberSystems.integerClass 1 0) =
              1
